title: Isa, prophet of Allah
hook: Muslims honor Isa, son of Maryam, as a great prophet and messenger who healed by Allah's leave
tomorrow: the one who left in anger

segments.voice: Yesterday, the baby who spoke from the cradle, and his mother's silence. Your line was let the truth speak. Did you say a little less? Day seventy-four.

Jesus is in the Qur'an. Not in a footnote: the name Isa comes up in surah after surah. His mother has a surah named after her. His birth, his first words and his miracles are all told. And when Muslims say his name, they add peace be upon him, as they do for the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the other prophets. So after three days in the story of his birth, today steps back and asks: who is Isa, for Muslims?
screen: `JESUS IS IN THE QUR'AN.` → `IN SURAH AFTER SURAH.` → `WHO IS ISA, FOR MUSLIMS?`

segments.voice: The Qur'an gives him titles. He is al-Masih, the Messiah. He is called a word from Allah, and a spirit from Him. He was given a scripture, the Injil, the Gospel. And one verse names him in a line with Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Muhammad, the five that tradition calls the messengers of firm resolve. Then there are his miracles. In Surah Al 'Imran, Isa speaks to his people and lists them: he shapes a bird from clay and breathes into it, and it becomes a bird. And then, in Pickthall's translation: “I heal him who was born blind, and the leper, and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave.” Listen for that last phrase, because it keeps coming back. By Allah's leave. By Allah's permission. In Arabic, bi-idhni llah. It appears again and again when the Qur'an describes what Isa did. The miracles are real, the Qur'an says, and they are Allah's. Isa is the one they come through. That phrase holds the heart of how Muslims see him: a great and beloved prophet, born of a virgin mother, a healer, and a servant of Allah, not Allah himself. Here the two neighboring faiths part ways, and it's worth saying plainly who believes what. Christians believe Jesus is the Son of God, that he died on the cross and rose again. Muslims honor him as a prophet and messenger, and the Qur'an says he was not killed or crucified, though it was made to appear so, and that Allah raised him up. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari speak of his return before the end. Both faiths honor him, and they understand him differently.
screen: `AL-MASIH: A WORD AND A SPIRIT.` · `THE BIRD OF CLAY, THE BLIND, THE DEAD.` · `BI-IDHNI LLAH: BY ALLAH'S LEAVE.` · `TWO FAITHS, TWO UNDERSTANDINGS.` · then, large: `A SERVANT OF ALLAH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: offer healing words to someone who's unwell. Settle, and breathe. Think of one person who is sick, or hurting, or worn down right now. Picture them clearly. What would help them hear? Not advice. Something kind. I'm thinking of you. You're not alone. I'll bring dinner Thursday. Choose the words. If you pray, you can ask Allah to heal them, since the healing is His. Then, when the bell ends, send those words. The bell holds the time.
Isa. Jesus, son of Maryam: in Islam, the Messiah, a great prophet and messenger, who healed by Allah's leave.

Your line: by Allah's leave. Today, when something you do goes well, remember it came through you, not only from you. That closes Maryam and Isa: a vow, a whisper, a messenger, a palm tree, a cradle, a healer. Tomorrow, a man who left in anger. Day seventy-four.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Isa as one of the messengers of firm resolve, say 'peace be upon him' after his name, and read his story in Surahs Al 'Imran, Al-Ma'idah and Maryam.

pairs: shaped, breathed on, and it flew

myth: Jesus is not mentioned in the Qur'an
Isa is named in surah after surah, and a surah is named for his mother.
the Qur'an credits Isa's miracles to Allah's permission
by Allah's leave, again and again (3:49; 5:110).
Muslims believe Isa is the son of God
Muslims honor him as a prophet and messenger; Christians believe he is the Son of God.

fork.setup: Isa stands before people who doubt him. he has healed the blind and raised the dead. how does he describe it?
options: I did this by my own power.
I did this by Allah's leave.
fork.reveal: I heal him who was born blind, and the leper, and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave (3:49).

original.note: Arabic: Isa, the Qur'an's name for Jesus, son of Maryam.

trapdoor: what you thought: Muslims don't believe in Jesus.
what it means: Muslims honor Isa as the Messiah and a messenger of firm resolve, a healer who worked by Allah's leave.
what a scholar hears: he is one of the ulu l-'azm, the messengers of firm resolve, called kalimatullah, a word from Allah (4:171); and 5:110 repeats bi-idhni, by My leave, four times.

sources.quoted: I heal him who was born blind, and the leper, and I raise the dead, by Allah's leave.

sources.ref: Qur'an 4:171 (the Messiah, a word and a spirit from Him)
Qur'an 4:157–158 (not killed or crucified; raised to Allah)

notes: Pickthall 3:49 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording.
Counts: Isa named about 25 times; Muhammad named 4 times (plus 'Ahmad' once). Stated as 'around twenty-five' and 'more often than the Prophet is named'. Confirm.

The Christian and Muslim beliefs are stated side by side without ranking (Son of God, cross and resurrection; prophet, 4:157–158, raised, many expect his return). Confirm wording with both a Muslim Keeper and, if wanted, the Christian path's Keeper.
'Among the greatest messengers' (ulu l-'azm: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, Muhammad) follows the common reading of 46:35 and 33:7; confirm.
5:110 'by My leave' count of four: confirm (clay bird, breathing, healing, raising the dead).
